findings.reason: adding `s4:["...#s2"]` (or s3) to `plan-section-depends-on` changes the dispatch order, and without it a worker either stalls ad hoc on §2 or substitutes its own notion of "kept", which is the one decision §2 exists to make.
findings.text: §4's candidate test and done-when measure imports against "kept scripts and benchmarks", which §2's census defines (and §3 realizes), yet §4 declares only §1 as a section dependency, so it can be released and scan a tree where that set is not yet established — with the census absent, a module imported only by a script §2 will keep is one the scan can miss or misjudge, and a module imported only by a script §2 will delete is held back for the wrong reason.

response_events.note: plan-section-depends-on now gives s4 both s1 and s2, so the deletion node is released only after the census that defines kept scripts and benchmarks has landed.

wiring-1.note: plan-section-depends-on now gives s4 both s1 and s2, so the deletion node is released only after the census that defines kept scripts and benchmarks has landed.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the six equilibrium modules §0 cites resolve at the stated line counts (5,861 / 4,172 / 4,125 / 3,570 / 3,295 / 2,969 against the 5.9k–3.0k quoted), the `docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/` convention exists with 32 sibling directories, and S28 resolves to `docs/plans/sub-millisecond-forward-path.html` (S28, active).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §1–§6 states a record with measurable contents and names a negative control that can fail (an unimported module reading zero, a live-test driver forced to delete refused, a kept file naming a deleted path, a reached module offered for deletion, a perturbed input exceeding tolerance, a non-executed module added to the written route).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every record lands under the durable `docs/evidence/fragments/code-reuse-and-hot-path/` directory (§1's `hot-path-map.html` with its machine-readable copy beside it, §2's `bench-scripts-census.html`, §3's per-batch `bench-scripts-delete-<n>`, §4's `unreached-module-delete.html`, §5's `hot-path-duplicates.html`), never a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no sprint id, plan label or ticket number reaches a code symbol; S28/S33 appear only in plan prose and decision metadata, and `nova/equilibrium/AGENTS.md` is named by what it documents.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the `s28-handoff` decision's rationale holds: `plan-informs` names `sub-millisecond-forward-path` and `inverse-equilibrium-baseline` one-way, so no declared relationship carries an S28 answer back, and §5 ("this section does not wait for it") and §6 ("as measured at this section's head") both read consistently with the chosen option.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section carries one deliverable; §3's several batches are dispatched as separate nodes, so no node closes on two verdicts at once.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §4's done-when scans for importers among "kept scripts and benchmarks", a set §2's census produces, but the declared dependency map gives §4 only §1 (`s4:["code-reuse-and-hot-path#s1"]`), so nothing orders §4 behind the set its own check consumes.
